title: Zooming in on a filling tank
stem: A sensor models water depth by $d(t)=12+0.8t+0.06t^2$ centimetres, where $t$ is in seconds. A technician uses the interval from $t=5$ to $t=5+h$ to estimate the rate at $t=5$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate for $h=2$. Give units.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that the average rate for any non-zero admissible $h$ is $1.4+0.06h$. Hence find the instantaneous rate.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For positive $h$, find the largest interval length that gives an estimate within 0.015 cm/s of the instantaneous rate.

steps.text: Use the change in depth divided by 2.

subject: math-aa-hl

verification.method: Independent recalculation and mark allocation review
verification.notes: Original 2027–28 cohort practice. Each marking point corresponds to the named part.

title: A calibration limit
stem: During a calibration the output is $S(t)=30+12t-3t^2$ for $0≤t≤4$. Engineers accept the model while its output is increasing and its instantaneous rate is at least 3 units per second.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the times for which both conditions hold.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A straight-line estimate from $t=1$ to $t=2$ has slope 3. Explain why the whole interval cannot be accepted.

steps.text: Solve $12-6t≥3$, which also implies an increasing output.
The instantaneous slope decreases over the interval.
